examples.en: Smear the wheel with pitch! Turn the wheel, the pitch is burning. The dear craftsman built the wheel, the wheel is good. The chariot is light.

examples.en: In the house of Boar there are two horses, three bulls, seven sheep, and a piglet. In the field of Crane are a hundred sheep. Boar said: "Your flock is big. May Perkʷunos guard it."

examples.pie: h₁yód h₂énHe gerh₂énes upér péth₂ōnti kʷíd ǵérh₂ontes mluHénti? ḱód mluHénti. h₁yód gerh₂énes péth₂ōnti sríHgos gʷm̥sḱéti. tód h₁sónt? tód h₁sónt. gerh₂énn̥s liméni dʰǵʰyés widóm. dóru dṓm h₁n̥dó bʰére. h₁íd bʰérōh₂.

examples.pie: h₂éwsōs h₂wést. bʰéwdʰesi? nu bʰéwdʰoh₂. h₁eǵʰ gʷm̥dʰí sóh₂wl̥-kʷe widé.

root.gloss: to sing; to produce a tune (such as music); to call or cry out

examples.pie: kʷís te doḱéyet? méh₂tēr me kéh₂nmn̥h₂ doḱéyet. swésōr moy ḱlutós kéh₂ntōr. h₁ésyeh₂s moy kéh₂nmn̥ kh₂né. nu h₂ḱh₂owsyé.
examples.en: Who taught you? Mother taught me songs. My sister is a famous singer. Sing me her song! Then listen well!

examples.pie: kʷértrom te pr̥sḱóh₂. kéh₂nmn̥ moy pinḱdʰí. h₁íd pinéḱmi. kéh₂nmn̥ ḱludʰí. túH kéh₂ntōr. h₁eǵóh₂ werdʰokʷr̥tḗr kéh₂nmn̥h₂-kʷe wékʷesh₂.
examples.en: Machine, I ask you: write a song for me! I am writing it. Hear the song! You are a singer! I am a word-maker, and songs are words.

examples.pie: túH kéh₂ntōr? h₁eǵóh₂ ne kéh₂ntōr. swésōr moy wékʷsperoy gʷéHyeti h₂óweyes-kʷe h₁íh₂m̥ ḱléwsonti. h₂óweyes sméyn̥ti? ne sméyn̥ti légʰyonti-kʷe.
examples.en: Are you a singer? I am not a singer. My sister sings in the evening, and the sheep listen to her. Do the sheep laugh? They do not laugh; they lie down.

source.name: coinage
source.note: Agent noun in -tōr from keh₂n- 'sing' (kéh₂ntlom 'song'): Lat. cantor 'singer' has the root and suffix.

source.name: coinage
source.note: Result noun in -mn̥ 'what is woven' from tek- 'weave' (as wésmn̥ 'garment' from wes- 'dress'), modelled on Gk ὕφασμα 'woven fabric' (Od.) to ὑφαίνω and Lat. textum 'woven cloth' to texō. The lexicon's wébʰos (Gk ὕφος 'fabric') is not used: Beekes 2010 s.v. ὑφαίνω calls ὕφος a late back-formation.
